# 2 Baruch Chapter 39 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 39 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 39:5 — "convict / expose / rebuke"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "will-convict-him-of-all-his-wickedness" | Forensic sense: the Messiah acts as judge |
| LOGOS | "will convict him of all his wickedness" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "will expose all his wickedness" | Slightly different — revealing rather than judging |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "convict" (EMET/LOGOS). The Syriac verb has a forensic/judgment sense — the Messiah is acting as judge, not merely as revealer.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 39:6 — "kill / execute / slay"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "will-kill-him" | Literal: basic kill verb |
| LOGOS | "will kill him" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "will execute him" | Forensic continuation — execution after conviction |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "will kill him." While PNEUMA's "execute" nicely continues the forensic imagery from v.5, the Syriac uses a simple kill verb here.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 39:7 — "principate / dominion / reign"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his-principate" | Latin-derived term for sovereign rule |
| LOGOS | "his dominion" | More natural English |
| PNEUMA | "his reign" | Most accessible modern term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "his dominion." "Principate" is overly technical; "reign" is fine but LOGOS's "dominion" preserves the scope of the Syriac shultana (authority/dominion).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
